Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Nov 20, 2026
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Allie Carl/Axios
 

Cleaning out the notebook as we await Anthropic's first full day of trading...

⏱️ Lag defense: On Monday, thousands of U.S. banking customers had difficulty accessing their accounts and making transactions because of a technical issue that began at JPMorgan Chase.

  • What if something like this (or more widespread) had happened a few days later and Anthropic IPO investors weren't able to pay for their allocated shares?
  • I asked some investment bankers about it, and they all admitted it was a problem they hadn't previously considered.
  • Some argued that the process could be saved by Wall Street's one-day settlement period (T+1) — obviously depending on the payment glitch specifics — and wondered if this would reduce enthusiasm for T+0.
  • That said, there also was a sense that Anthropic may still have paused its process to avoid the flood of legal work if share prices declined and investors tried to cancel their contracts before transfers went through.

🥇 Largest IPO ever: Anthropic officially broke the IPO record briefly held by SpaceX, after underwriters exercised greenshoe options to purchase more shares. The total raise comes out to $93.54 billion, not including the $26 billion concurrent private placement.

🚪 Behind the scenes: I'm told that the Claude maker never seriously considered the SpaceX strategy of picking a set share price and sticking with it, instead wanting the investor feedback and price discovery that comes via the classic bookbuilding process.

  • It also got a big confidence boost very early in the process, when large mutual funds put in allocation requests on Day 1.
  • That's common for hedge funds that are seeking to develop a relationship with company management, but not for mutual funds that typically view themselves as having leverage.

💵 Price talk: There's an argument to be made that Anthropic did its IPO at a Goldilocks price. Enough of a pop that IPO buyers are in the black, but not so much that the company (and its bankers) look like they left a fortune on the table.

  • The counter, of course, is the headline risk tied to shares closing below the first trades and opening down another 9% this morning. Yes, IPOs are just a moment in time. But declining share prices can make it harder to hire and hurt internal morale (just ask anyone at Facebook post-IPO).
  • For Anthropic, there's also all the counterfactuals about what would have happened had it not priced into an absolutely miserable trading day. And also questions about whether some of the declines were caused by rotation into Anthropic, although the declines likely were too broad to conclude causation.

⚡ Permit pass: The Senate last night passed the bipartisan permitting reform bill known as BAAJA. It now heads to the House, where Speaker Mike Johnson says it has enough votes to pass.

  • Axios' Ben Geman writes: "The eyes of the entire energy industry are on this bill. If it becomes law, it could transform how America builds energy infrastructure, with major implications for everything from electricity costs to data centers."

❓ Quiz time: Can you name the PE big whose departure had less to do with spending more time with family than the time he was spending with a subordinate? Hint: This also became an issue for some of the firm's LPs.

📺 ICYMI: We've posted full videos of Axios BFD conversations with Vista Equity's Robert Smith, the NY Fed's John C. Williams, Goldman Sachs' Kim Posnett, baseball legend Alex Rodriguez, Lowercarbon Capital's Chris Sacca, Kalshi's Tarek Mansour, Capital One's Lia Dean with Maria Sharapova, Blackstone's Joan Solotar, and 1789 Capital's Omeed Malik & Donald Trump Jr.

🌎 Where in the world: I'll be at the Boston Public Library at 12:30pm today to chat biz news with Jim and Margery on Boston Public Radio. Couches, coffee and conversation. Stop by if in the neighborhood.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios
 

Sanofi (Nasdaq: SNY) is weighing an acquisition offer for Insmed (Nasdaq: INSM), a New Jersey-based drugmaker focused on respiratory diseases, per Bloomberg.

Why it's the BFD: It would be the largest biotech deal in three years.

Market reax: Insmed shares jumped 20.6% on the news, driving its market cap to $31.7 billion. Sanofi shares fell more than 2%.

The bottom line: "Some investors and analysts warned that the likely price would stretch Sanofi's resources, though several also welcomed a move to offset the looming loss of exclusivity of Dupixent, the blockbuster skin and asthma drug that has fueled the company's growth." — Ashleigh Furlong & Sonja Wind, Bloomberg
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

Payward, owner of crypto exchange Kraken, acquired venture capital firm Tribe Capital — which was co-founded by Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi.

• Variational, an on-chain derivatives trading protocol, raised $110m in Series B funding at a $1.5b valuation. Bain Capital Crypto led, joined by Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV, and 50T Funds. axios.link/48rWSpt

• Acutronic Group, a Swiss-American drone maker, raised $100m. InterAlpen Partners and Hale Capital Partners led, joined by ICOR Group and Pictet Alternative Advisors. axios.link/4ztxdYj

• Linq, an SF-based infrastructure platform for AI agents, raised $90m in Series B funding. A16z led, joined by TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, Abstract, Anthos, and Left Lane Capital. axios.link/4zDj6jt

• Everful, a wholesaler that connects smaller retailers with Chinese factories, raised $48.5m in Series A funding. Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital led, joined by Square Peg and Lightspeed. axios.link/3XCkSUm

• Braid, a Dutch enterprise connectivity platform, raised $38m in Series A funding. Octopus Ventures led, joined by KPN Ventures. axios.link/4zX0Geb

• Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street-food chain, raised $18m in Series B funding. Left Lane Capital led, joined by BIG Capital and insider Titan Capital. axios.link/4zXQrGH

• Metano, a San Jose, Calif.-based agentic security startup, raised $12m in seed funding. Sierra Ventures led, joined by Correlation Ventures, High Alpha, and 360 ONE. axios.link/4B59rmX

• InPrime Finserv, an Indian non-bank lender, raised $10.7m in Series B funding. FMO led, joined by Z47 and Pravega Ventures. axios.link/3VD4CSz

• Archer (fka hackajob), a U.K. recruiting platform, raised $10m. Volition Capital led, joined by insider AVP. axios.link/4kx2S7D

• Disseqt AI, an Irish AI governance and assurance startup, raised $8m in pre-Series A funding. Gresham House Ventures led, joined by Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, and Enterprise Ireland. axios.link/4zSETEw

• MountAIn, a French developer of AI infrastructure for microcontrollers, raised €7.3m in seed funding. 360 Capital and Supernova Invest led, joined by Crédit Agricole Alpes Développement. axios.link/48rX8EX

• Modern Industrials, an NYC-based workflow automation platform for manufacturers and distributors, raised $6m in seed funding. Glasswing Ventures and TMV led, joined by a16z speedrun. axios.link/4l8CdOq

• Hoplite, an AI agent swarm startup, raised $5.5m from YC, John and Patrick Collison, Paul Graham, Des Traynor, Zach Sims, Relational Capital, Upside Ventures, and Theo Browne. axios.link/4AD1LI6

• Eight by Zero, a Canadian insurance interoperability platform, raised C$3m in seed funding led by Diagram and joined by Canada Life. axios.link/3WYom3k

• Touchmark, a market and management platform for AI inference and compute, raised $3m in seed funding from Inception Fund, YC, Liquid 2 Ventures, Kima Ventures, RedBird X, Pareto Holdings, and Spot VC. axios.link/4klUjwe

🚑 IntelliProve, a Belgian contactless health-monitoring startup, raised €2.7m in seed funding. Miles Ahead led, joined by Wit-Gele Kruis and imec.istart. axios.link/4tbTOqZ
 
 
Private Equity Deals
 

• EQT agreed to buy Australian auction house Pickles from Apax Partners. axios.link/4l0pKfJ

• Falfurrias acquired Freeman & Forrest, a B2B influencer marketing firm. axios.link/4iYHJk3

• Lyte Fiber, backed by SDC Capital Partners, acquired MSEC Communications (dba MidSouth Fiber) from MidSouth Electric Cooperative. axios.link/49aJaHy

• Permira and Freeman Spogli agreed to buy a majority stake in Brunt Workwear at a valuation north of $800m. The Wilmington, Mass.-based workwear brand had raised over $40m in VC funding from firms like Stripes and TF Cornerstone. axios.link/4j05NTF

🚑 TJC agreed to acquire a majority stake in HMP Global, a health care events and education firm, from Susquehanna Growth Equity (which retains a minority position). Axios Pro flashback

• TPG agreed to buy a majority stake in business payments firm Bill Holdings (NYSE: BILL) for around $6b, or $63.25 per share, with Corpay (NYSE: CPAY) taking a minority stake. axios.link/4zCMne3

• Transom Capital Group completed its $114m take-private buyout of public safety tech company SoundThinking. axios.link/4rE1Nwc

• Turnspire Capital Partners acquired outdoor cooking equipment maker Middleby Outdoor from Middleby (Nasdaq: MIDD) and merged it with portfolio company GHP Group. axios.link/4zTkCyJ

• Wynnchurch Capital completed its $463m take-private buyout of U.K. materials maker Luxfer. axios.link/3TkO0xv

• xFact, a Renovus Capital Partners portfolio company, merged with Mission Critical Partners, a provider of consulting and managed services to public safety and other government groups. axios.link/4krZ3R6
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

⚡ Presidio Production (NYSE: FTW) agreed to acquire Permian Basin-focused oil and gas assets of Rusmore Resource Partners, a portfolio company of Trace Capital Management, for $360m. axios.link/3WWsv7Y
 
 
More M&A
 

🐒 Bending Spoons (Nasdaq: BSP) agreed to buy email automation company Mailchimp from Intuit (Nasdaq: INTU) for $3.68b. axios.link/4zZ8Jao

• Bluespring Wealth of Austin acquired Dynasty Advisors, a Freehold, N.J.-based firm managing approximately $1.6b in client assets. axios.link/3UFqNqY

⚡ DOJ closed its antitrust investigation of NextEra Energy's (NYSE: NEE) $67b planned acquisition of Dominion Energy (NYSE: D). axios.link/4tdNlvE

• Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. (NYSE: AJG) acquired AgriServ, a Panora, Iowa-based specialist crop insurance broker. axios.link/4zunqkZ

• Rockwell Automation (NYSE: ROK) agreed to acquire AGILOX, an Austrian developer of autonomous mobile robots. axios.link/4kntnfD

• Oliver Wyman, the management consulting business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), agreed to acquire Synpulse, a Swiss financial-services technology consultancy. axios.link/4j5Wphm
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Shane Shannon, most recently an advisor to the Treasury Department's general counsel, is joining Macquarie as a managing director in its private credit and infrastructure debt business, Axios' Courtenay Brown has learned.
